question: What does an infrared thermometer primarily detect to measure body temperature?

options.A: Electrical resistance of the skin surface
options.B: Chemical reactions inside the probe cover
options.C: Direct conduction of heat from the blood
options.D: Thermal radiation emitted by the body

explanation: Infrared thermometers capture the invisible thermal energy radiating from body tissues and convert it into a digital reading. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: Why are infrared thermometers preferred over traditional glass thermometers in busy triage units?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any infection control
options.B: They never require calibration or battery replacements
options.C: They provide absolute internal core temperature values
options.D: They deliver fast temperature readings within seconds

explanation: Rapid measurement times allow nurses to screen large volumes of patients quickly during emergency triage. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: Which internal component of an infrared thermometer absorbs radiated energy and creates a voltage?
explanation: The thermopile absorbs the focused infrared radiation and converts that thermal energy into an electrical voltage. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the internal compensation sensor in an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Adjusting readings based on ambient room temperature
options.B: Sterilizing the probe tip between patient uses
options.C: Cooling down the lens after multiple rapid tests
options.D: Amplifying the battery voltage for the display screen

explanation: Compensation sensors measure surrounding environmental conditions so the device can adjust the calculation for accurate surface measurement. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why is the tympanic membrane an ideal site for measuring core body temperature?

options.A: It shares a blood supply with the hypothalamus
options.B: It is the thickest mucous membrane in the body
options.C: It produces large amounts of protective earwax
options.D: it is completely unaffected by ambient room air

explanation: The eardrum and the brain's temperature control center share common blood vessels, making ear readings very close to core temperature. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: A nurse is using a temporal artery thermometer on an adult patient. How should the device be moved?

options.A: Slid vertically down the center of the nasal bridge
options.B: Placed under the tongue and left until it beeps
options.C: Pressed firmly and held stationary inside the auditory canal
options.D: Swept across the forehead and down behind the earlobe

explanation: Proper temporal scanning requires moving the sensor smoothly across the forehead and touching the skin behind the ear to capture peak perfusion. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is the effect of impacted cerumen in the ear canal on a tympanic temperature reading?

options.A: It causes a dangerously high fever reading
options.B: It has no effect on the infrared sensor output
options.C: It stops the thermometer from turning on completely
options.D: It causes a falsely low temperature reading

explanation: Earwax blocks the thermal rays coming from the eardrum, preventing the sensor from detecting the true internal heat. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h4)

question: Which clinical situation is a contraindication for using a temporal artery thermometer?

options.A: Heavy perspiration or bandages across the forehead
options.B: Fasting for routine laboratory blood investigations
options.C: A history of mild uncomplicated hypertension
options.D: A mild cough and productive respiratory secretions

explanation: Moisture from sweating cools the skin via evaporation, and bandages trap heat or block the sensor, causing inaccurate measurements. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h4)

question: How should a nurse position the ear of an adult patient before inserting a tympanic probe?

options.B: Pull the pinna up and back
options.C: Push the pinna forward against the face
options.D: Tilt the head sharply toward the chest

explanation: Pulling the adult ear up and back straightens the curved ear canal so the infrared sensor has a clear line of sight to the eardrum. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h5)

question: A nurse prepares to take a child's temperature using a tympanic thermometer. What action must be done right after the reading?

options.A: Immerge the entire electronic device in bleach
options.B: Place the thermometer back in the patient's pocket
options.C: Blow forcefully onto the glass lens to cool it
options.D: Discard the disposable probe cover safely

explanation: Used probe covers must be removed and thrown away immediately to prevent cross-contamination between patients. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h5)

question: Why might a patient lying on one side for hours show a higher temperature in the upper ear?

options.A: Pressure changes damage the inner ear mechanics
options.B: Heat gets trapped and accumulates in that ear
options.C: Blood flow to the brain completely stops during sleep
options.D: The lower ear is always colder due to gravity

explanation: Pillows and bedding insulate the side of the head against the bed, causing local heat retention in the exposed ear canal. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the effect of a dirty, smudge-covered lens on an infrared thermometer?

options.A: It converts the thermometer into a mercury-based scale
options.B: It automatically increases the battery life of the device
options.C: It has no impact on the final digital display value
options.D: It blocks infrared transmission and causes inaccurate readings

explanation: Obstructions on the sensor lens interfere with the thermal rays entering the device, leading to false measurements. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: What cleaning solution is typically recommended for wiping down an infrared thermometer body and lens?
explanation: Isopropyl alcohol disinfects the surface effectively without leaving residue or destroying the plastic casing when used correctly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: What is a major risk of submerging an infrared thermometer in liquid disinfectant?

options.A: The plastic casing changes color to bright yellow
options.B: The battery compartment permanently locks shut
options.C: Fluid enters and damages internal electronic circuits
options.D: The temperature scale shifts from Celsius to Fahrenheit

explanation: These devices are not waterproof; liquid seeping inside shorts out the internal motherboard and sensors. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: What critical detail must a nurse include when documenting an infrared temperature reading in patient notes?

options.A: The room temperature of the hospital ward
options.B: The brand name of the plastic probe cover
options.C: The serial number of the thermometer device
options.D: The specific anatomical measurement site used

explanation: Recording the site (tympanic or temporal) is essential because normal ranges vary depending on where the body heat was captured. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h8)

question: Why is it important to compare a new temperature reading against a patient's baseline trends?

options.A: Fever thresholds are identical for every human being
options.B: Hospital regulations forbid recording standalone single numbers
options.C: Digital thermometers lose accuracy after twenty-four hours
options.D: Individual baseline temperatures vary among different healthy people

explanation: Normal body temperature differs from person to person, so tracking personal trends helps identify subtle signs of infection early. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h8)
